---
title: Express integration
nav: Express
description: Mount the ClipMux handler in an Express app with toNodeListener, before any body parser.
---

`clipmuxHandler` is a Fetch handler: it takes a `Request` and returns a
`Response`. `toNodeListener` from `@clipmux/node/express` adapts it to
Node's `(req, res, next)` shape, so one Express route answers the uploader,
the player and ClipMux's webhooks.

[`examples/express`](https://github.com/visheshgubrani/clipmux/tree/main/examples/express) is a whole app built this way.

## Before you start

- An Express app on Node 20.19 or later.
- The packages, and your app connected with `init`, which writes the
  `CLIPMUX_*` settings to `.env.local` (or `.env`, if you have one and no
  `.env.local`):

<Tabs items={['npm', 'pnpm']}>
<Tab value="npm">

```bash
npm i @clipmux/node @clipmux/uploader @clipmux/player
npx @clipmux/node init --server https://video.example.com
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="pnpm">

```bash
pnpm add @clipmux/node @clipmux/uploader @clipmux/player
pnpm dlx @clipmux/node init --server https://video.example.com
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

`new ClipMux()` reads the settings from `process.env`, so load the env file
before the handler runs, for example with `node --env-file=.env.local`.

## Mount the route [#mount-the-route]

```ts
import { clipmuxHandler } from '@clipmux/node/handlers'
import { toNodeListener } from '@clipmux/node/express'
app.post('/api/clipmux/:action', toNodeListener(clipmuxHandler({ … }))) // before express.json()
```

The `{ … }` holds your `upload`, `playback` and `asset` callbacks, exactly as
in the [quickstart](/docs/build/quickstart)'s route file. The route answers
POSTs to `/api/clipmux/upload`, `/api/clipmux/playback` and
`/api/clipmux/webhook`.

<Warning>
  Mount it before `express.json()`. The webhook's signature covers the raw
  body, and a body another middleware already parsed can't be checked. If
  the route must come later, give it `express.raw({ type: '*/*' })`. A body
  parsed into an object is refused with an error that says so.
</Warning>

Each callback gets a Fetch `Request`, not Express's `req`. Read cookies and
headers from `req.headers`, and query parameters from `new URL(req.url)`.
The handler reads the body itself: the upload's `file` and the player's
`playbackId` are in the callback's second argument.

An error the adapter can't turn into a response goes to Express's `next`,
so your error middleware sees it.

## Add the elements

In any page your app serves, load the two elements and point them at the
route:

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@clipmux/uploader/element'
  import '@clipmux/player/element'
</script>
<clipmux-uploader create-url="/api/clipmux/upload?lesson=42"></clipmux-uploader>
<clipmux-player playback-id="pid_…" session-url="/api/clipmux/playback"></clipmux-player>
```

The bare imports need a bundler, or an import map that points
`@clipmux/uploader/element` and `@clipmux/player/element` at the files in
`node_modules`.

## Fastify and plain node:http

The same listener runs wherever Node's request and response objects are.
On plain `node:http`, route to it yourself:

```ts title="server.ts"
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { clipmuxHandler } from '@clipmux/node/handlers'
import { toNodeListener } from '@clipmux/node/express'

const clipmux = toNodeListener(clipmuxHandler({ /* upload, playback, asset */ }))

createServer((req, res) => {
  if (req.url?.startsWith('/api/clipmux/')) return clipmux(req, res)
  res.statusCode = 404
  res.end()
}).listen(3000)
```

In Fastify, pass it the raw request and response, `request.raw` and
`reply.raw`. The listener reads the body from the raw request, so Fastify
must not have read it first.

## Check it works

```bash
npx @clipmux/node doctor
npx @clipmux/node listen --forward-to localhost:3000/api/clipmux/webhook
```

`doctor` ends with `✓ Ready.` Upload a file from your page; when it's
encoded, `listen` prints `✓ video.asset.ready ast_… → 200`.

- `listen` shows `500`, and your server logs `the request body was already
  parsed`: the route is after `express.json()`.
- `listen` shows `400`: the secret is wrong, or the body was changed before
  the handler read it.
